title: Dropbox acquires Tigris Data for $350M to bolster its AI infrastructure
slides: Dropbox just paid $350M for Tigris Data — why now?
Tigris builds storage that scales for AI workloads
Yet Dropbox's core business has nothing to do with AI training
Your shared files may soon sit on AI-optimized infrastructure
Watch whether Dropbox ships AI features or just rents storage
thread_text:
1. Dropbox's $350M AI Bet

Dropbox just bought Tigris Data for $350M. Tigris builds storage for AI workloads — a world away from your shared folders.

2. AI Storage, Not File Sharing

Tigris scales for AI training and inference. Dropbox's core product? Storing your PDFs and photos. The two don't overlap.

3. Your Files on AI Infrastructure

Your shared links may soon live on AI-optimized storage. That means faster access but also new terms you never agreed to.

4. Rent vs. Build

The real question: will Dropbox ship its own AI features, or just rent Tigris's tech? One adds value, the other adds margin.

5. Test the AI Claim

This week, open Dropbox and look for one new AI feature. If you can't find it, you'll know it's just storage.
